title: Door clearance as BCF: from a verdict to an issue the architect can open

host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named.

turns.request: Check every door in the Duplex against the 850 mm clear-width rule, DC-W1, and show me the model coloured by verdict.
turns.reply: 14 doors: 8 Pass and 6 Fail. The four 762 mm leaves (two on Level 1, two on Level 2) fail by 88 mm, and the two 813 mm leaves (Level 1) fail by 37 mm. The six 864 mm leaves (Level 2) pass by 14 mm and the two 1250 mm leaves (Level 1) by 400 mm. The check reads each door's OverallWidth, the proxy that NRC's rule DC-W1 uses for clear width, so it measures the leaf and not the opening. In the 3D view the failing doors are blue and the passing ones orange.

turns.request: Compare that with NRC's ground truth for the test kit.
turns.reply: All 14 doors agree: the tally has 14 rows where the verdict matches the file's ExpectedVerdict_ClearWidth850, and none where it differs. The file's OverallWidthMm also equals the graph's width on every row. The doors to watch are the ones a tolerance would flip. The 813 mm doors, Revit element ids 171853 (1s1jVhK8z0pgKYcr9jt781) and 171975 (1s1jVhK8z0pgKYcr9jt7AB), fail by 37 mm, so any allowance of 37 mm or more would pass them. The six 864 mm doors, element ids 150378, 150478, 159734, 159834, 160065 and 160208, pass by 14 mm, so a required margin of more than 14 mm would fail them. The file below is NRC's door_ground_truth.csv, byte for byte.

turns.request: Turn the six failing doors into BCF issues for the architect. Show me the topics before anything is written.
turns.reply: Six topics, one per failing door, each naming one element: the four 762 mm doors (88 mm short) and the two 813 mm doors (37 mm short). I chose one topic per door over one topic for all six because an architect works through a BCF list door by door. Status and comments belong to a topic, so a door can be closed once its leaf is changed while the others stay open, and each topic's viewpoint will frame its own door instead of all six. The title carries the level and the Revit family name with its element id, for example the last of the four 762 mm doors ends in 204034, which is how a Revit user finds a door; the description gives the width and the shortfall. The Status column is empty in the preview because the writer supplies Open. If the 762 mm doors are fixed by one type change, one topic per type is the other sensible grouping; samples/nrc/bcf/dc-w1-failures.bcf (graph bcf-from-ids-failures) is the single-topic form.

The BCF writer is an effect, so it runs only on Run, and this notebook does not Run graphs. I ran nb-s14-door-bcf-issues through the host and copied the file the Run wrote into the repository: samples/nrc/bcf/s14-door-bcf-failures.bcf, 6 topics, 6 viewpoints, 6 elements, none without geometry, 8,531 bytes. Each topic holds one viewpoint: its door selected, and a camera that frames that door. The BCF is a version 3.0 file, and the library's tests validate files written by the same writer against the buildingSMART BCF 3.0 schemas (DuplexBcfTests, BcfCameraCommentTests in bim-open-data); no BCF viewer was run on this file. The bytes are repeatable: the graph fixes the topic creation time (created 2026-10-18T22:00:00Z) and the guidSeed, and gives no model date, so a second Run writes the same file; I ran it three times and the SHA-256 did not change. The size and SHA-256 on the card are those of the committed file.

turns.request: A reviewer wants to comment on the two 813 mm doors, the near-threshold ones, from a camera outside the building. Add that comment and write it as its own BCF.
turns.reply: One issue on both doors, one row per door in the table. Title "813 mm doors: 37 mm under the 850 mm rule", author Reviewer, with the comment text in the Comment column. The camera columns hold the viewpoint: position (24, -24, 12), a direction toward the middle of the two doors, and a 60 degree field of view. It is set by hand here with view3d.camera; the 3D pane's Comment button builds the same two nodes from the camera on screen. The creation time is a parameter, 2026-10-18T23:00:00Z, because bcf.issue reads no clock; bcf.write's created is the same instant, so the file does not depend on when it runs. Run wrote samples/nrc/bcf/s14-door-bcf-review.bcf: 1 topic, 1 viewpoint, 2 elements, 1,865 bytes. Its viewpoint uses this camera in place of a framed one, and the comment sits under the topic.

turns.request: The architect has replied in the BCF. Read the returned file, show me the comments, and colour the flagged doors in 3D.
turns.reply: The returned file, samples/nrc/bcf/s14-door-bcf-reply.bcf (1,991 bytes), holds the same topic with 2 comments by two authors: Reviewer, then Architect, who agrees and says a wider leaf type will come in the next revision of the model. The topic is still Open and names 2 elements; joined to the model on GlobalId they are the two Level 1 glass doors, Revit element ids 171853 and 171975, 813 mm, each Fail with 2 comments, and the 3D view paints them. Nothing in the model has changed: the verdicts still say Fail until a revised model is checked again. The architect's reply is staged for this walk-through, not a colleague's: the graph below, nb-s14-door-bcf-reply, writes it by joining the reviewer's row to a second bcf.issue under one title and one guidSeed, so a viewer would treat the file as an update of the reviewer's topic. The decision is not written back into the IFC in this notebook.
